description: Make concurrent EnsureModelHost reuse deterministic and correct by identifying whether the failure is a production ensure/reuse race or a test choreography race, correcting the owning Models runtime-host boundary, preserving the strict one-supervised-process invariant, and proving stability through 50 race-enabled repetitions and GOMAXPROCS variation.

context.customerAsk: Deflake TestEnsureModelHostConcurrentReuseSharesOneSupervisedProcess in pkg/services/models/internal/services/runtime_host/internal/service. Stress the package with 50 race-enabled repetitions and GOMAXPROCS variations, capture the failure mode, distinguish a production reuse race from a test synchronization race, state the exact interleaving in the PR, fix the responsible boundary without sleeps or weakened assertions, retain a strict regression when production is racy, and restore green CI.
context.problem: Backend Unit Coverage failed on main in CI run 31449874394 job 93651926054 because the concurrent model-host reuse test did not reliably prove that simultaneous EnsureModelHost calls share one supervised process. The suspected production window is between observing no existing load and publishing loading state, which may let multiple callers become starters; direct evidence must distinguish that logical race from faulty test choreography. The flake blocks unrelated work, and a production double-start could waste capacity, overwrite supervised state, or leave process ownership ambiguous.
context.solution: Use race-enabled repetition, controlled GOMAXPROCS variation, and deterministic gates around observable runtime-host or launcher state to capture the exact interleaving. Correct the smallest Models-owned boundary responsible for the failure. If production is racy, make the absent-to-loading election atomic so one caller starts the process and followers await the same terminal result, with a strict deterministic regression. If only the test is faulty, preserve production and coordinate the test with channels or wait groups. Keep public contracts unchanged and prove the focused package stable across 50 race-enabled repetitions and scheduler variations.

userStories.notes: Diagnosis completed on 2026-08-10. This is a production EnsureModelHost reuse race, not test choreography: callers A and B can both return nil from supervisor.go:123-128 while the shared supervisedRuntime is absent; A then publishes loading and loadDoneA at supervisor.go:130-147, while B enters the later lock, has no loading case, overwrites the state and loadDone with a second attempt, and starts a second supervised process. GitHub Actions run 31449874394/job 93651926054 reproduced the exact assertion at service_test.go:255 (process starts = 2, want 1). The baseline focused -race -count=50 run passed once, but an uncontrolled concurrent scheduler sweep reproduced the duplicate start; sequential GOMAXPROCS=1,2,8,32 runs at -race -count=50 all passed, confirming nondeterministic exposure rather than a test-only race. go test, go vet, make typecheck, and git diff --check passed. The owning boundary is Models runtime_host; atomic election and the deterministic regression are story 002 work.

userStories.title: Guarantee one shared supervised process
userStories.description: As an operator using a local model, I want simultaneous readiness requests for the same host to converge on one supervised process so capacity and lifecycle ownership remain correct.
acceptanceCriteria: For one runtime scope and model identity, concurrent callers elect or observe one loading attempt atomically, exactly one caller performs the process-start side effect, and other callers wait for and reuse that attempt's terminal result.

All successful callers receive a ready, loaded host snapshot from the shared process, and the service does not deadlock, lose wakeups, overwrite the active process, or leave an extra process unsupervised.

A deterministic concurrency regression coordinates callers at the diagnosed boundary and fails when the former double-start or unsafe test interleaving is restored; it asserts exactly one process start without sleeps or retries.

If diagnosis proves the production path was already correct, production behavior remains unchanged and only the test choreography is made deterministic through channels, wait groups, or observable launcher state.

Failure and cancellation from the elected readiness attempt remain observable to waiting callers according to existing runtime-host behavior, with process launch and stop effects still isolated behind the injected host process boundary.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented on 2026-08-10. `supervisedRuntime.ensureReady` now performs the ready/loading/failed observation and absent-to-loading election under one mutex-protected state transition; followers capture the elected attempt's `loadDone` channel and wait for its terminal result, so no caller can overwrite the active process or completion signal. Added a test-only `AfterLoadStateObservation` barrier and coordinated all eight callers after releasing the runtime-state mutex; the fixed path publishes loading atomically before followers observe it, while a temporary restoration of the former split implementation fails deterministically with `process starts = 8, want 1`, proving the regression pins the diagnosed gap. Every fixed-path caller receives a ready/loaded snapshot and the strict launcher assertion remains exactly one process start. Existing startup failure, cancellation, inspection, stop, unload, and distinct-slot tests remain green. No public API or generated contract changed. Focused reuse test passed with `-race -count=50`; full runtime-host package, race package run, vet, typecheck, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, and diff checks passed. Story 003 retains the scheduler-variation evidence and final stress-recording work.
